recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future changes to MedicationStatement.status for escape-valve or no-known-medication use cases should wait for final work-group decisions on the newer unresolved Jira issues, not be made under FHIR-5965.
issue_request: FHIR-5965 was a Published Pharmacy change request resolved as Persuasive with Modification. It reported that MedicationStatement.status timing values such as in-progress or completed could conflict with MedicationStatement.effective[x], and it asked whether the status semantics or an invariant should prevent illegal combinations.
initial_application: The seed was applied historically: Jira comments cite svn 6556 for status updates and svn 6745 for the status definition update; git history shows #5965 commits 097af202a4, 534313123a, and cf7b12afe7, with cf7b12afe7 changing the MedicationStatement.status definition to the approved patient/source judgment wording. The invariant question was moved to FHIR-8010.
additional_context: FHIR-8010 was later Published/Not Persuasive with Modification and clarified status/wasNotTaken semantics rather than adding a current invariant. Later Pharmacy decisions changed the current model: FHIR-19468 and FHIR-19470 moved taking/not-taking information into MedicationStatement.adherence, FHIR-32060 changed status codes to recorded, entered-in-error, and draft, and FHIR-39271 reaffirmed that status is recording status while adherence and effective[x] carry medication-use semantics. FHIR-55338 and FHIR-54315 are later unresolved or triaged discussions and do not change the applied/published model.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active current source defines MedicationStatement.status as recording status, limits it to recorded | entered-in-error | draft, directs taking/not-taking semantics to adherence, and uses effective[x] for the medication-taking interval, so the original status/effective conflict no longer exists in the current build.
